purpose: A STAAD-compatible schema for storing authorized, client-specific depression-related session observations and longitudinal context. Included example records are synthetic demonstrations only.
important_boundary: This package does not contain real client information and must not be used to infer or diagnose depression. Clinical knowledge belongs in the separate Depression Knowledge Memory; client memory must contain only provenance-linked information from authorized client/session sources.

node_types.description: Pseudonymous client reference; avoid direct identifiers in the graph.
Clinician/system-recorded observation, with source and timestamp.
Experience explicitly reported by the client; preserve attribution.
A documented mood/symptom concept, not a diagnosis by itself.
A documented contextual factor such as a life event or routine change.
An event reported or observed before an experience; not proof of causation.
Documented effect on daily activities, school, work, relationships, or self-care.
An intervention or strategy discussed/delivered by a qualified professional.
Client-reported or observed response to an intervention/activity.
A measure or progress note with method, date, and interpretation boundaries.
A tentative longitudinal pattern requiring review; never a diagnosis or proven causal claim.
A safety-relevant statement/event, with careful access controls and approved escalation workflow.
Transcript span, event, clinician note, or other provenance source.

design_rules: Use only authorized STAAD client/session sources for actual client memory.
Do not put general clinical facts or guideline passages into the client graph; those belong in Knowledge Memory.
Keep reported experiences distinct from clinician observations and model-generated summaries.
A pattern hypothesis must link to supporting source events, carry confidence/review status, and remain tentative.
A trigger or preceding event does not prove cause.
A symptom mention is not a diagnosis; diagnosis requires an appropriate qualified professional workflow.
Risk-related content must follow STAAD's approved human escalation and access-control workflow; the graph must not autonomously triage emergencies.
Apply least-privilege access, pseudonymization, retention/deletion policies, audit logging, and applicable legal/privacy review.
